stage_a.note: Strong positive expression; she smiles warmly while talking about loving dogs.
Sustained engagement; she speaks passionately about the importance of pet safety.
Friendly and approachable demeanor during the introduction and throughout the pitch.

venture.description: A crash-tested car safety harness for small dogs that secures them to the seat to prevent injury in accidents.
venture.note: The founders ask for $100,000 for 10% of Zugopet.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls introduces herself and her location.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn introduces herself, her location, and the two dogs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states the ask, describes the danger of unsecured dogs, and introduces the Rocketeer Pack.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert laughs at the video of the dog in the harness.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls acknowledges that the product looks unusual.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that the dog looks really happy in the harness.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert expresses disbelief at the product's appearance.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls reassures the panel that despite looking silly, it is the best option.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori interrupts to point out that the panel is laughing too hard to hear the pitch.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin expresses disbelief that the dogs in the video are real.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert continues to express amusement and disbelief.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls resumes the presentation and begins demonstrating how to attach the harness to the seat.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert asks if the dog is being velcroed directly to the car seat.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains that the velcro helps hold the dog in place while adjusting the other straps.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if the dog has been given drugs to stay so calm.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls assures Lori that the dog is fine and not drugged.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori questions how the dog can possibly be happy in that position.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark rhetorically asks what alternative would be better.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges the idea, stating that dogs prefer to stick their heads out the window.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls continues the demonstration, adjusting the straps and explaining the suspension protects the spine.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if the dog is scared while suspended in the harness.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn replies that the dog is just nervous about the pitch.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn points out that their product passed the same crash test that others failed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls mentions that the harness can also be used as a front or backpack carrier.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori compares the carrier feature to a baby carrier.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert agrees that the carrier feature is a great idea.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks if there are other similar dog seatbelt products on the market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls replies that they are the only company with a patent for this.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies his question, noting he has seen people strap dogs to bikes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls acknowledges other products exist but notes they are not crash-tested or safety-approved.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for the retail price of the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states that the harness costs one hundred and sixty dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert remarks that the price seems very high.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks how much it costs them to manufacture the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls replies that the manufacturing cost is thirty-six dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori notes that the product has a very large profit margin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks for their total sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states they have one hundred and eighty thousand dollars in sales since launching in November.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks which channels they are using to sell the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls replies that they currently sell exclusively through their own website.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how they are driving customer traffic to their website.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains that their traffic is entirely organic and driven by word of mouth.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks how the founders came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn explains she developed it for her dog with joint injuries because nothing else was available.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls adds that she licensed the product from Carolyn because she believes in it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks how much money Juls has invested in Carolyn's business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states she has invested a total of two hundred thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what the invested money was used for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls explains the funds went toward crash testing, production, and two hundred thousand dollars in inventory.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond asks who is responsible for the daily operations of the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls states that she runs the day-to-day business operations.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what Carolyn's role in the business is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls replies that Carolyn handles all the order fulfillment from her garage.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks for statistics on how many dogs are killed in car accidents annually.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Carolyn admits she does not know the number but notes UK laws regarding unsecured dogs in accidents.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if they are currently selling the product in the United Kingdom.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls confirms they sell the product in forty different countries.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin challenges their sales volume, suggesting they must have sold very few in each country.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls defends the product by emphasizing they are one of only three companies to pass the crash test.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert challenges the product's convenience, stating it takes too long to put a dog into the harness.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls counters by asking if Robert takes the time to secure his children in the car.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Robert exits, stating he would not spend the time to secure a dog this way.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin exits, stating the business is too early and not worth the requested million-dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori exits, explaining that the product looks too complicated and needs to be simplified.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Daymond exits, stating that while he appreciates the mission, the business is too early for him.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark exits, advising them to improve their marketing by selling against the fear of accidents.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Juls thanks the investors for their time and feedback.

decisions.note: He doesn't want anything to do with it because it takes too long to put the dog in.
He thinks it's too early, not investable yet, and not worth a million dollars.
She thinks the product looks complicated and needs to be simpler to use.
He thinks they don't have everything figured out yet and it's a little too early.
He thinks their marketing isn't good and they need to sell against fear.

record.notes: The presentation includes a demonstration of securing the dog in the harness, which prompts several questions from the panel before the formal Q&A begins. The panel is highly amused by the dog's appearance in the harness.
